note: Every setting has exactly one true source (Brett, Nov 18 2026: "All settings need one true fucking source."). A setting key (or key pattern) maps to one owning store: a data-store@1 namespace + path (the document) and a JSON pointer inside it. Readers resolve through the owner (framework/core/settings-source.mjs, apps/console-web/server/settings_source.py); a write to any other store is refused; `mirrors` must be empty on every entry (CI: framework/cli/check-settings-sources.mjs). Spec: framework/spec/SETTINGS-SOURCES.md. Filled from the three audits (_claude/builds/reports/one-true-source-for-every-setting/audit-*.json) and duplicates.md.

storeKinds.data-store: a data-store@1 key (`ns` + `path`): the document lives where framework/schemas/data-store-paths.json puts it today and on axf-data once its namespace is cut over; readable and writable from Node and Python
storeKinds.browser: a SettingsRegistry (framework/core/settings.ts) saved under `storageKey` in the app's localStorage; readable only inside that app, so the owner's control is the app's Settings and the API path is console-control@1 (control@1 for tokens)

storeFields.ns + path: the data-store@1 key (path may use the key's {n} captures)
storeFields.file: where the document is today: a template over the four data roots {plugins} {data} {repo} {projects} and the key's captures; absent = the data-store key's own file
storeFields.envDir: an env var that moves the whole folder (the owner's own override, e.g. AXF_PIPELINE_DIR)
storeFields.envFile: an env var that names the file itself
storeFields.frame: the document's $axf, written when the resolver creates it
storeFields.owner: the plugin or module that writes it
storeFields.editor: the console_show deep link of the one control that edits it
storeFields.api: REST route, MCP tool, CLI and voice action: the four surfaces of that one control. `rest` is written relative to the owner's API root (a plugin's routes live under its plugin API: `<verb> <route>`), never as an absolute path

entryFields.key: the setting's global name or pattern (* one segment, trailing ** the rest)
entryFields.pointer: JSON pointer inside the owner document ({1}.. captures, {rest} flat, {rest/} nested, "" whole document)
entryFields.derive: optional: `not-in-list:{n}` = the value is true when the captured name is absent from the array at the pointer (a write adds / removes it)
entryFields.readers / writers: who reads (through the owner) and who may write
entryFields.formerly: where copies used to be: { store, pointer, note }; the migration strips them and the check refuses writes there

pointerNote: `pointer` is a JSON pointer inside the owner document. `{1}`, `{2}` are the key's `*` segments in order; `{rest}` is what `**` matched as one pointer segment (dots kept: a flat document keyed by dotted names); `{rest/}` is the same with `.` turned into `/` (a nested document). Pointer "" means the whole document.
